heading: INT. FUNERAL HOME - CASKET SHOWROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. FUNERAL HOME - CASKET SHOWROOM - DAY
Mahogany, pine, brushed steel.
Satin linings in six shades of cream.
A single armchair for the grieving.
A small fountain gurgles in the corner.
AUGUSTUS PEMBROKE (50s, widower in training, black suit too tight at the shoulder) walks the room with his hat in both hands.
He stops at the cheapest casket and touches it with one finger, as though it might be hot.
A SALESMAN (40s, shiny shoes, a lapel pin shaped like a dove) appears out of nowhere at his elbow.
Good morning, sir. Have you lost someone?
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Ah. A planner. I admire a planner.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: My wife's still alive. She's in the car.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: In the car.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: She's got a cold. She wanted to wait.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Of course. We offer a drive-through option, sir, for the living.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: Really?
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: No.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: Augustus nods slowly.
The Salesman leans on the pine casket and pats it, as a man pats a horse.
This is our Starter. Pine, plain handles, a one-year warranty.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: On a casket?
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: If it fails, we replace it. Free of charge.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: How would you know it failed?
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Sir, that is exactly the question my own father asked.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: What did you tell him?
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: That we have a very friendly staff. My name is Percival, by the way.
units.name: SALESMAN

units.text: Augustus.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Augustus. May I ask what your wife would want?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: She'd want me to stop pricing things.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: She sounds lovely.
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: She's insufferable. She's alive.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Then why are you here?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: Because she told me to. She said, Gus, pick something so I don't have to hear about it.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Ah. A woman who delegates. I'd like to meet her.
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: She'd like to meet you too. She's been waiting forty minutes.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: In the car?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: In the car.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Percival straightens.
He glances at the door, then back, and for the first time he looks worried.
Sir, you left her in a parked vehicle with a cold?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: With the heater on.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: How long?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: I told you. Forty minutes.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Forty minutes in a car with the engine running?
units.name: PERCIVAL

units.text: Oh.
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: They look at each other.
Then they both run for the door, Augustus knocking over the fountain, Percival clutching his dove pin, a pair of grown men in dark suits sprinting through a showroom of empty beds.
